newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - April 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - April 28.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Police continues island-wide search for Pai Hsiao-yen, kidnapped daughter of famous actress and hostess Pai Ping-ping.
Wu Poh-hsiung, secretary-general of ruling Nationalist Party, says party's constitution revisions are flexible.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - Taiwan studies direct telephone links across Taiwan strait.
Police finds car of Pai Hsiao-yen's kidnappers.
LIBERTY TIMES - Premier Lien Chan orders island-wide search for Pai Hsiao-yen.
Nationalist Party expects to pass constitution reform package during provisional central committee meeting.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - U.S. memory board maker Kingston Technology Corp to invest US$100 million in Taiwan for memory board production and establishing ventures.
Taiwan's quality of life ranks seventh in Asia.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Foreign investors to be allowed to invest in convertible bonds.
Taiwan to open satellite businesses for private participation.
